leads.claim: Lt. Brown obtained samples of an unidentified substance from Mr. Dahl and Mr. Crisman that were allegedly related to a flying disc.
leads.why: The document explicitly links specific individuals (Dahl, Crisman, Brown) to the transfer of physical samples alleged to be from a UAP.
leads.government_response: AAF Intelligence officers collected the samples; later, the government investigated the claims and concluded the material was a hoax.
leads.material_description: Samples of an unidentified substance/lava oxide metal.
leads.quote: Lt Brown obtained from Mr. Dahl and Mr. Crisman samples of an unidentified substance

leads.claim: Specimens of an alleged flying saucer were brought to Wright Field for analysis by the Analysis Division (T-2).
leads.why: The document confirms the physical transfer of alleged UAP material to a military laboratory for technical analysis.
leads.custody_chain: FBI to Lt. Col. Garrett to T-2 Analysis Division at Wright Field
leads.government_response: Technicians at Wright Field analyzed the specimens and determined they were a hoax made of plaster of paris and electrical wire.
leads.material_description: Fragments of undeterminable shape made from plaster of paris or ceramic containing electrical resistance wire.
leads.quote: The specimens of an alleged Flying Saucer brought to this Command by Colonel H. M. McCoy

doc_verdict: The document contains detailed accounts of the government obtaining and analyzing physical material alleged to be from a UAP, though the government's own investigation concluded these specific instances were hoaxes.
